bib.title: Large language models encode clinical knowledge

read.skipped: Supplementary Information (hyperparameters, prompts, per-size tables) is not in the PDF; Extended Data tables/figures are images with only captions in text.

question: Can LLMs (PaLM, Flan-PaLM) answer medical questions well, and how should answers be evaluated beyond multiple-choice accuracy?
hypothesis: Scale, instruction tuning and a small amount of in-domain instruction prompt tuning will improve medical QA and close the gap to clinicians on safety-relevant axes.
contributions: MultiMedQA benchmark: 6 existing datasets plus new HealthSearchQA (3,173 questions)
Pilot human evaluation framework (clinician and lay axes)
SOTA on MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA, MMLU clinical topics with Flan-PaLM 540B
Instruction prompt tuning and the resulting Med-PaLM

method.summary: Evaluate PaLM and Flan-PaLM (8B/62B/540B) on MultiMedQA with few-shot, CoT and self-consistency prompting, then align Flan-PaLM 540B to consumer medical QA by learning a soft prompt (instruction prompt tuning) on 65 clinician exemplars to produce Med-PaLM. Long-form answers are rated by clinicians and lay users.

datasets.name: MMLU clinical topics
datasets.size: test: anatomy 135, clinical knowledge 265, college medicine 173, medical genetics 100, professional medicine 272, college biology 144

datasets.name: LiveQA (TREC 2017)
datasets.split: questions sampled for human eval and prompt-tuning exemplars

datasets.name: HealthSearchQA
datasets.split: 100 random questions used in human eval; exemplars disjoint
datasets.source: search-engine suggested questions from seed conditions and symptoms; released with paper

datasets.name: Instruction prompt tuning exemplars
datasets.split: sampled from HealthSearchQA, MedicationQA, LiveQA; answers by 5 clinicians, filtered

other.pretraining: 780 billion tokens, exactly one epoch; 540B on 6,144 TPUv4 chips

models.name: Med-PaLM
models.architecture: Flan-PaLM 540B with learned soft prompt prefix

other.soft_prompt: p x e matrix; p and hyperparameters in Supplementary section 2 (not in PDF)

training.objective: negative log-likelihood on 65 exemplars; only soft prompt (p x e matrix, random init) trained, LLM frozen; soft prompt is prefix before hard task prompt

other.note: hyperparameters deferred to Supplementary Information section 2

inference.decoding: temperature sampling for self-consistency; majority/plurality vote
inference.samples: self-consistency 11 CoT decodes per question; selective prediction used 41 decodes; reporting summary says MedQA experiments repeated independently three times
inference.prompting: Dataset-specific few-shot prompts written with clinicians; typically 5 input-output examples for consumer QA, 3 or fewer for PubMedQA; CoT prompts clinician-crafted (Supplementary sections 11, 12)

metrics.name: clinician axes
metrics.definition: consensus alignment, incorrect/missing content, harm extent and likelihood (AHRQ-inspired), bias, comprehension/retrieval/reasoning evidence

eval.protocol: 140 questions (100 HealthSearchQA, 20 LiveQA, 20 MedicationQA); answers from Flan-PaLM, Med-PaLM, clinicians, source blinded; 9 clinicians (USA, UK, India), 5 lay raters (India), one rater per answer; non-parametric bootstrap, 1,000 replicas, 95% percentile interval

availability.data: MultiMedQA incl. HealthSearchQA released as supplementary file

results.note: Abstract says 'more than 17%'; text says 17.3% over PubMedGPT and 20.1% over DRAGON (47.5).

results.claim: Flan-PaLM 540B scores 62.0% on the harder 5-option MedQA.
results.setup: Flan-PaLM 540B, few-shot/CoT/self-consistency prompting, MultiMedQA multiple-choice test sets; MedQA 5 options

results.claim: Flan-PaLM 540B reaches 57.6% on MedMCQA dev-test, above Galactica.
results.setup: Flan-PaLM 540B, few-shot/CoT/self-consistency prompting, MultiMedQA multiple-choice test sets; MedMCQA development-test
results.quote: Flan-PaLM 540B reached a performance of 57.6% on

results.claim: Flan-PaLM 540B reaches 79.0% on PubMedQA, 0.8 above BioGPT; single-rater human is 78.0%.
results.setup: Flan-PaLM 540B, few-shot/CoT/self-consistency prompting, MultiMedQA multiple-choice test sets; PubMedQA

results.claim: Flan-PaLM 540B gets 83.8% on MMLU professional medicine and 80.4% on clinical knowledge.
results.setup: Flan-PaLM 540B, few-shot/CoT/self-consistency prompting, MultiMedQA multiple-choice test sets; MMLU professional medicine subset (clinical knowledge 80.4)
results.quote: Flan-PaLM 540B achieved a state-of-the-art accuracy of 83.8%

results.claim: Self-consistency (11 CoT decodes) improves MedQA by more than 7% over few-shot, but drops PubMedQA.
results.quote: we observed an improvement of more than 7% with self-consistency

results.claim: CoT prompting gave no improvement over standard few-shot on MedQA, MedMCQA, PubMedQA.
results.quote: We did not observe improvements using COT over the standard few-shot prompting strategy

results.claim: Scaling PaLM and Flan-PaLM from 8B to 540B gives about 2x accuracy; Flan-PaLM 540B beats 62B by >14% and 8B by >24%.
results.quote: We observed an improvement of approximately 2× in performance when scaling the model from 8B to 540B

results.claim: Instruction tuning: 8B Flan-PaLM beats 8B PaLM on PubMedQA by over 30%.
results.quote: 8B Flan-PaLM model outperformed the baseline PaLM model by over 30%

results.claim: Selective prediction: deferring 45% of MedQA questions by self-consistency agreement raises accuracy on the rest to 82.5%.
results.setup: Flan-PaLM 540B, CoT + self-consistency with 41 decodes, MedQA; deferring fraction 0.45
results.note: Quote is the hyphenated line; sentence: 'ing an accuracy of up to 82.5% at a deferring fraction of 0.45 (Fig. 3)'.

results.claim: Clinicians judged 61.9% of Flan-PaLM long answers aligned with scientific consensus vs 92.6% Med-PaLM and 92.9% clinicians.
results.setup: 140 consumer questions (100 HealthSearchQA, 20 LiveQA, 20 MedicationQA); 9 clinician raters, one rating per answer; Med-PaLM 540B
results.quote: 92.6% of Med-PaLM answers were judged to be in accordance

results.claim: Potentially harmful answers fell from 29.7% (Flan-PaLM) to 5.9% (Med-PaLM); clinicians 5.7%.
results.quote: this number fell to 5.9% for Med-PaLM

results.claim: Med-PaLM answers contained inappropriate or incorrect content in 18.7%, worse than Flan-PaLM (16.1%) and clinicians (1.4%).
results.quote: with 18.7% of the Med-PaLM answers judged to contain inappropriate

results.claim: Omission of important information fell from 47.6% (Flan-PaLM) to 15.3% (Med-PaLM); clinicians 11.1%.
Bias (answer inapplicable to a demographic) in 7.9% of Flan-PaLM answers vs 0.8% Med-PaLM; clinicians 1.4%.
results.setup: same 140-question human evaluation; yes/no single question
results.quote: this number decreased to 0.8% for Med-PaLM

results.claim: Lay raters found 60.6% of Flan-PaLM answers helpful vs 80.3% Med-PaLM and 91.1% clinicians.
results.setup: 5 lay raters in India, same 140 questions, one rater per answer
results.quote: this increased to 80.3% for Med-PaLM answers

results.claim: Evidence of correct knowledge retrieval: clinicians 97.8%, Flan-PaLM 76.3%, Med-PaLM 95.4%.
results.quote: the instruction prompt-tuned Med-PaLM model scored 95.4%

limits: Single rater per answer and only 140 questions in human evaluation
Rating axes pilot, subjective; harm scale (AHRQ) not validated for this context
Bias evaluation is narrow; most questions neutrally framed
English only; multiple-choice easier than real clinical workflows
Models may reflect past scientific consensus
Effect of instruction prompt tuning on multiple-choice accuracy not fully analysed (preliminary only, Extended Data Table 5)
Possible memorisation of datasets; overlap analysis in Supplement found minimal overlap
Med-PaLM answers had more incorrect content than Flan-PaLM (18.7% vs 16.1%)
Model weights and code not released; Med-PaLM not reproducible; hyperparameters only in Supplement
Clinician-authored exemplar and prompts from small panels
